observations.title: The repository documents its own architecture in-tree
observations.question: Read these before writing anything about this repository's architecture. Which of them state a convention that is a correctness requirement rather than a style preference, and which name a footgun a newcomer would hit? Anything already written here belongs in AGENTS.md as a CITATION, never as a paraphrase that will drift from the original.
observations.draft_rule: Before changing `<area>`, read `<doc path>` — it is the authored convention for this subsystem. State the constraint it carries (`<constraint>`) and cite the document rather than restating it here.

observations.title: This repository defines or consumes an inter-process interface (D-Bus / IDL / protobuf)
observations.question: Which of these definitions does this repository OWN, and which are copies or generated proxies of a definition owned elsewhere? Who are the peers on the other side of the interface, and what happens to them when a signal, method or field changes here?
observations.draft_rule: The interface definitions under `<paths>` are owned by `<owning repo>`. Never edit a generated proxy — change the canonical definition and regenerate with `<command>`. A change to a method, signal or field is a cross-repository change: name the affected peers (`<repos>`) in the PR and land the coordinated change before merging. Relevant catalogue skills: `ultimaker-firmware-development`.

observations.title: This repository participates in the G/M-code command contract
observations.question: Does this repository SEND, FORWARD or HANDLE these codes? A code is a contract shared by every repository on its path — which sibling has the parser, which has the dispatcher, and which document is the registry of record?
observations.draft_rule: Adding or changing a G/M-code is an ecosystem change, never a local one. Register the code and its parameter definitions in `<registry path>` and synchronise the parser, dispatch and handler in `<sibling repos>` in the same ticket. Load `ultimaker-gcode-architecture` before touching a code; do not restate the registry in this repository. Relevant catalogue skills: `ultimaker-gcode-architecture`.

observations.title: This repository is a provider or consumer in a submodule graph
observations.question: For each submodule: does this repository merely consume it, or does it own it? Who else pins the same submodule, and what is the ordering discipline when a change spans both trees (innermost first, push the submodule branch before moving the parent pointer)?
observations.draft_rule: Submodule pointers in this repository are moved only after the corresponding change is merged and pushed in `<submodule repo>`. Never commit inside a submodule tree from this checkout. A pointer bump is its own commit and names the upstream revision it moves to.

observations.title: Tests are collected in a top-level test tree
evidence: 11 test files: 9 in a central tree, 2 beside sources
observations.question: Should the test-placement convention be stated so agents stop guessing where a new test belongs?
observations.draft_rule: Place new tests in the top-level test tree, mirroring the source directory structure.

observations.title: Commits are small and tightly scoped
observations.question: Should the scope rule name a concrete file-count expectation derived from this repository's own history?
observations.draft_rule: Keep commits tightly scoped: this repository's median commit touches 1 files. A commit touching more than 3 files needs an explicit justification in the message.

observations.title: Observed file-size distribution (input to the ratchet)
evidence: 1 of 27 sampled files exceed the 400-line budget and will be grandfathered at their current size
observations.question: The file-size ratchet is already generated as a managed rule (`10-file-size-and-decomposition-rules.md`) with a 400-line budget. Is 400 the right budget for this codebase, or does its shape justify a different number (90th percentile is 262)? Re-run the bootstrap with `--file-size-budget N` to change it — do not write a competing rule.
observations.draft_rule: No new rule needed: adjust the managed budget instead. Consider whether the largest grandfathered files deserve a decomposition ticket of their own.

observations.title: File names are predominantly PascalCase
observations.question: Does the convention differ per language or per directory, and is it worth stating so new files match?
observations.draft_rule: Name new source files in PascalCase, matching the existing tree.

observations.title: Commit subjects are kept short
observations.question: Is a hard subject-length limit worth stating explicitly?
observations.draft_rule: Keep commit subjects at or below 72 characters.
